Way back in 2007, Iaonnidis and Trikalinos proposed the Test of Excess Significance (TES).
More recently, Stanley and Doucouliagos (2021) proposed some tweaks to TES that allow for heterogeneity and try to correct the conservatism of the original TES. 
All of these tests are defined in terms of the number of affirmative (positive and statistically significant) effect sizes observed in a meta-analysis and the number of affirmative results one would expect to see given the average effect size and degree of heterogeneity.

Consider a random effects model in which effect size parameters are normally distributed with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\tau$. 
Under the random effects model and for a given study with standard error $\sigma_i$, the observed effect size estimate $T_i$ is normally distributed with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sqrt{\tau^2 + \sigma_i^2}$. Letting $A_i$ be an indicator for whether $T_i$ is statistically significant based on a one-sided test at level $\alpha$, the probability that the observed effect size estimate is affirmative (i.e., the power of study $i$) is 
$$
\pi_i = \text{Pr}(A_i = 1 | \sigma_i) = 1 - \Phi\left(\frac{\sigma_i \Phi^{-1}(1 - \alpha) - \mu}{\sqrt{\tau^2 + \sigma_i^2}}\right),
$$ {#eq-power}
where $\Phi()$ and $\Phi^{-1}()$ are the standard normal cumulative distribution function and quantile function, respectively.

Stanley and Doucouliagos (2021) proposed the PSST, which is pretty much the same thing as TES but allowing for heterogeneity in the effect size distribution. The PSST test statistic is
$$
Z_{PSST} = \frac{\bar{A} - \bar\pi}{\sqrt{\bar\pi(1 - \bar\pi) / k}},
$$ {#eq-Z-psst}
where $k$ is the number of observed effect sizes, $\bar{A} = \frac{1}{k} \sum_{i=1}^k A_i$ is the proportion of observed effect sizes that are affirmative, and $\bar\pi = \frac{1}{k} \sum_{i=1}^k \pi_i$ is the average power across all $k$ studies.
The TESS test statistic is 
$$
Z_{TESS} = \frac{\bar{A} - \bar\pi - 0.05}{\sqrt{0.05 \times 0.95 / k}}.
$$ {#eq-Z-tess}
Stanley and Doucouliagos also propose that PSST and TESS should be used together, so one would reject the null of no publication bias if either PSST or TESS exceeds a one-sided standard normal critical value, $\Phi^{-1}(0.95)$.

I am a bit perplexed about how PSST and TESS are derived, so I'm going to use a simple model to study them. Let's assume that $\bar{A}$ is approximately normally distributed. In the absence of publication bias, $\bar{A} \cdot\sim N\left(\bar\pi, \frac{1}{k} \bar{V}\right)$, where $\bar{V} = \frac{1}{k} \sum_{i=1}^k \pi_i(1 - \pi_i)$. It follows that $Z_{PSST}$ will exceed $\Phi^{-1}(0.95)$ if $\bar{A} - \bar\pi$ exceeds $\Phi^{-1}(0.95) \times \sqrt{\bar\pi(1 - \bar\pi) / k}$, and so the Type I error rate of the PSST will be approximately
$$
\text{Pr}\left(Z_{PSST} > \Phi^{-1}(0.95) \right) = 1 - \Phi\left(\Phi^{-1}(0.95) \times \sqrt{\frac{\bar\pi(1 - \bar\pi)}{\bar{V}}}\right).
$$ {#eq-TypeI-PSST}

Under the same assumptions, the Type I error rate of TESS will be approximately
$$
\text{Pr}\left(Z_{TESS} > \Phi^{-1}(0.95) \right) = 1 - \Phi\left(\frac{0.05}{\sqrt{\bar{V} / k}} + \Phi^{-1}(0.95) \times \sqrt{\frac{0.05 \times 0.95}{\bar{V}}}\right).
$$ {#eq-TypeI-TESS}
This is a more complex curve, which can exceed the nominal .05 level for some values of $\bar{V}$ and $k$. For a given value of $\bar{V}$, the Type I error rate decreases for larger $k$.

For the combined PSST-TESS test, the null will be rejected if the maximum of $Z_{PSST}$ and $Z_{TESS}$ exceeds $\Phi^{-1}(0.95)$, equivalent to the condition that 
$$
\bar{A} - \bar\pi \geq \min \left\{\Phi^{-1}(0.95) \times \sqrt{\bar\pi(1 - \bar\pi) / k}, \ 0.05 + \Phi^{-1}(0.95) \times \sqrt{0.05 \times 0.95 / k} \right\}.
$$
It follows that the Type I error of the combined test is the maximum of the power of the separate tests,
$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Pr}\left(Z_{PSST} > \Phi^{-1}(0.95) \right) &= \max \left\{\text{Pr}\left(Z_{PSST} > \Phi^{-1}(0.95) \right), \ \text{Pr}\left(Z_{TESS} > \Phi^{-1}(0.95) \right) \right\} \\
&= 1 - \min \left\{\Phi\left(\Phi^{-1}(0.95) \times \sqrt{\frac{\bar\pi(1 - \bar\pi)}{\bar{V}}}\right), \ \Phi\left(\frac{0.05}{\sqrt{\bar{V} / k}} + \Phi^{-1}(0.95) \times \sqrt{\frac{0.05 \times 0.95}{\bar{V}}}\right) \right\}.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-TypeI-PSST-TESS}


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
TESS_typeI <- function(Vbar, k) {
  pnorm(
    0.05 / sqrt(Vbar / k) + qnorm(0.95) * sqrt(0.05 * 0.95 / Vbar),
    lower.tail = FALSE
  )
}

TESS_error <- 
  expand_grid(
    Vbar = seq(0.01,0.25,0.005),
    k = seq(10,50,5)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    error = pmap_dbl(., TESS_typeI)
  )

ggplot(TESS_error) + 
  aes(Vbar, error, color = factor(k)) + 
  geom_line()
```
